newsitem.title: USA: Hess to pay $5.3 mln environmental fine.
newsitem.headline: Hess to pay $5.3 mln environmental fine.

text.p: A refining unit of Amerada Hess Corp agreed to pay $5.3 million in fines and restitution after pleading guilty to ferrying hazardous waste from a Virgin Islands refinery to Arizona.

Hess Oil Virgin Islands Corp shipped some 300 tons of a spent oil-refining catalyst containing benzene between Dec. 11, 1991, and Feb. 9, 1992 to Arizona, where it was sold to a cement manufacturer, a Hess Oil spokesman said on Thursday.
The spokesman described the shipments as an oversight.

The federal government will receive $3 million of the Hess payments, a government official said. The balance will be divided among Texas, which will get $300,000; Pima County, Arizona, which will receive $1 million; and the Virgin Islands. The Virgin Islands will use its $1 million to build a household hazardous-waste program.
Hess, whose St. Croix oil refinery is the largest in the western hemisphere, plead guilty in a federal court in Newark, New Jersey, on Tuesday.
